questions.question: A train 125m long passes a man running at 5km/hr in the same direction in which the train is going, in 10 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.explanation:
Speed of train relative to man = Distance/Time = 125/10 m/s = 12.5 m/s
Converting to km/hr: 12.5 × 18/5 = 45 km/hr (relative speed)
Relative speed = Speed of train - Speed of man
45 = Speed of train - 5
Speed of train = 50 km/hr
questions.shortcut: Relative speed = 125m / 10s = 12.5 m/s = 45 km/hr relative. Add man's speed: 45 + 5 = 50

questions.question: Two stations A and B are 110 km apart on a straight line. One train starts from A at 60 km/h and another from B at 50 km/h. How long will it take for the two trains to meet?
questions.explanation:
When trains move towards each other:
Relative speed = 60 + 50 = 110 km/hr
Distance between them = 110 km
Time = Distance / Relative Speed = 110 / 110 = 1 hour
questions.shortcut: When moving towards each other, add speeds. 110/(60+50) = 110/110 = 1 hour

questions.question: An article was sold at a loss of 12%. If it was sold for Rs.880, what was the cost price?
questions.explanation:
Let CP = x
Selling Price (SP) = 880
Loss = 12% means SP = 88% of CP
880 = 0.88x
x = 880/0.88 = 1000
Cost Price = Rs.1000

questions.question: If a merchant sells an article at a loss of 8%. Had he sold it for Rs.56 more, he would have gained 6%. What is the cost price?
questions.explanation:
Let CP = x
At 8% loss: SP₁ = 0.92x
At 6% gain: SP₂ = 1.06x
Difference: 1.06x - 0.92x = 56
0.14x = 56
x = 400
CP = Rs.400
questions.shortcut: Difference in selling prices = (6% + 8%) of CP = 14% of CP = 56. CP = 56/0.14 = 400

questions.question: What is the simple interest on Rs.2500 at 8% per annum for 2 years?
questions.explanation:
Simple Interest = (Principal × Rate × Time) / 100
SI = (2500 × 8 × 2) / 100
SI = 40000 / 100 = Rs.400
questions.shortcut: SI = PRT/100. Memorize: 2500 at 8% for 2 years = 400

questions.question: What is the compound interest on Rs.8000 at 15% per annum for 2 years?
questions.shortcut: CI formula: A = P(1+R/100)^n. For 8000 at 15% for 2 years ≈ 2580

questions.question: If the price of an item increases from Rs.400 to Rs.500, what is the percentage increase?
questions.explanation:
Percentage increase = ((New Value - Old Value) / Old Value) × 100
= ((500 - 400) / 400) × 100
= (100 / 400) × 100
= 25%

questions.question: If A:B = 2:3 and B:C = 4:5, what is A:B:C?
questions.explanation:
A:B = 2:3 means A=2k, B=3k
B:C = 4:5 means B=4m, C=5m

For B to be same: 3k = 4m
If k=4, then B=12. So A=8
If m=3, then B=12, C=15
Therefore A:B:C = 8:12:15
questions.shortcut: Multiply first ratio by 4, second by 3 to make B same: (8:12) and (12:15) = 8:12:15

questions.question: If 6 men can do a piece of work in 12 days, how many men are required to do the same work in 8 days?
questions.explanation:
Work = Men × Days (constant)
6 × 12 = M × 8
72 = 8M
M = 9 men
questions.shortcut: Inverse proportion: More days needed = fewer men. 6 × 12 = M × 8, so M = 72/8 = 9

questions.question: The HCF of two numbers is 11 and their LCM is 7700. If one of the numbers is 275, find the other.
questions.explanation:
Formula: HCF × LCM = Product of two numbers
11 × 7700 = 275 × x
84,700 = 275x
x = 84,700 / 275 = 308
questions.shortcut: Always remember: HCF(a,b) × LCM(a,b) = a × b

questions.question: What is the next number in the series? 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, 42, ?
In how many ways can 5 different books be arranged on a shelf?
questions.explanation:
Arrangement of n different objects = n!
5! = 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120 ways

questions.question: A die is rolled once. What is the probability of getting a number greater than 4?
questions.explanation:
Numbers greater than 4 on a die: 5, 6 (2 outcomes)
Total outcomes = 6
Probability = Favorable outcomes / Total outcomes = 2/6 = 1/3
questions.shortcut: Die outcomes > 4: only 5 and 6. That's 2 out of 6 = 1/3

questions.question: The average of 5 consecutive odd numbers is 55. What is the largest number?
questions.explanation:
5 consecutive odd numbers with average 55
Middle number = 55 (in 5 consecutive numbers, middle one is average)
Numbers: 51, 53, 55, 57, 59
Largest = 59
questions.shortcut: For consecutive numbers, average = middle value. So largest = middle + 2×2 = 55 + 4 = 59
